item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Retirement of Translate slides in PowerPoint Live
item.description:
[What and why]

Starting November 30, 2026, attendees in Microsoft Teams meetings will no longer be able to translate slides into another language in PowerPoint Live by using Change view > Translate slides. Other PowerPoint Live features for presenters and attendees are not affected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Retirement (Worldwide): Beginning and completing in late November 2026
  • Translate slides will be removed for all attendees on November 30, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Attendees who use Translate slides in PowerPoint Live during Microsoft Teams meetings

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams meetings
  • PowerPoint Live

What will happen

  • Attendees will no longer see the Translate slides option in PowerPoint Live under Change view > Translate slides.
  • Attendees will see slides in the language in which they were created.
  • Presenting with PowerPoint Live and other attendee viewing options are not affected.
  • There is no admin setting to manage this change.
  • No admin action is required.
  • Most organizations will see little impact because only a very small share of PowerPoint Live sessions use this option.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to prepare for this change. Translate slides will be removed automatically for all attendees on November 30, 2026.

We recommend that you:

  • Notify presenters and users in your organization about this change, especially teams that present to audiences who speak different languages.
  • Ask presenters to share slides in the languages their audiences need ahead of time.
  • Update internal training or help content that mentions Translate slides in PowerPoint Live.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Onboarding workflow for new team members
item.description:

Microsoft Teams is introducing an onboarding workflow that helps new team members get started faster by automatically connecting them to relevant channels when they join a team. This can improve engagement, accelerate onboarding, and make important information easier to find from the start.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 573452.

[Rollout Schedule:]

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Automatically add tag members to channels with Workflows
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have clarified the supported channel types and updated the rollout timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app to automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag. Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually. This is especially useful for location-based or project-based groups where tags correspond to specific sites, regions, or projects, helping new members access relevant channels promptly.

This applies to channels that all team members can access by default: standard channels and shared channels that are shared with everyone on the team.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release (R3.6): Rollout will proceed gradually from November 2026 through January 2027.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-March 2027 (previously mid-December 2026) and is expected to complete by end of March 2027 (previously mid-December 2026).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams users who are added to team tags associated with configured workflows.
  • Team owners who choose to configure the workflow.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Workflows app
  • Power Automate

What will happen

  • The Join member to channel when user is added to tag template will be available in the Workflows app.
  • When configured, the workflow will automatically add users to selected channels when they are added to a team tag.
  • Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

Joining new tag members to channels

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted. Team owners can configure the workflow at any time if desired.

[Compliance considerations]

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available. For any tenant that unifies app/agent availability through Phase 1, Phase 2, or Phase 3, app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

  • App and agent availability unification (Section A): Rollout began in late September 2025. The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.
  • App and agent installation unification (Section B): Released. Installation unification completes within 24–48 hours after a tenant completes app availability unification(Section A) in Phase 1, 2, or 3

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

For tenants with agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, a wizard in the Teams admin center will help identify affected agents and apps and guide through resolving discrepancies.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unified app and agent installation management 

This capability unifies installation management across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Administrators can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, with changes synchronized across both admin centers. 

Who receives this capability? 

Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible. Once rollout begins, this capability will be automatically enabled for tenants whose availability is already unified as part of Section A. Tenants that unify their availability later will receive this capability automatically once unified. 

Note: This capability is separate from availability unification described in section A . It does not automatically unify app or agent availability. 

When will it roll out? 

Rollout will begin at the end of September 2026 for eligible tenants. This date applies only to installation management (section B). 

Is administrator action required? 

No additional action is required to enable installation unification for eligible tenants. Existing installation assignments for supported apps and agents will be synchronized across both admin centers. 

Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

item.title: [stayInformed] Continuous interpreter visibility with pop out video in Teams
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Users who work with sign language interpreters in Microsoft Teams meetings will be able to pop out their paired interpreters' video into a separate window. The window can be resized and moved anywhere on the screen, including to another monitor. Interpreters stay in view while users multitask, share content, or change meeting layouts. This is designed for Deaf and hard-of-hearing (D/HH) users, for whom losing sight of an interpreter means losing access to the conversation.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid January 2027 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This applies to Teams desktop on Windows and Mac. After this rollout, users can:

  • Pop out their paired sign language interpreters' video into a dedicated window that stays on top of other apps.
  • Resize the window and move it anywhere on their screen or to another monitor.
  • Keep interpreters in view while presenting, viewing shared content, using chat or captions, or with the main meeting window minimized.

The pop-out window only changes the user's own view, and interpreters stay in the main meeting gallery for everyone else. The window isn't visible to other participants when the user shares their screen.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

You don't need to do anything to prepare. Consider telling D/HH users and the interpreters who support them about this feature, and update your training and accessibility documentation as needed. To use the feature:

  1. In Teams Accessibility settings, turn on Sign language mode and select I am a Signer.
  2. Select Manage interpreters and add the people who interpret for you.
  3. Select View > Pop out interpreters during a meeting.
  4. Users open the pop-out window in each meeting. For faster access, they can pin the Pop out interpreters button to the meeting toolbar. There is no admin policy for this feature.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Real-time queue metrics in the Queues app on Mobile
item.description:
[What and Why:]

For calling representatives and supervisors, staying informed about call queue activity is important to managing incoming calls and maintaining timely customer service. However, when working away from their desks, they may not have visibility into current queue conditions, such as how many calls are waiting or how effectively calls are being handled. Without this information, it becomes harder to respond to changing call volumes and make informed decisions about queue participation.

We're introducing real-time call queue metrics in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams Mobile. Calling representatives and supervisor leads can now monitor key operational metrics directly from their mobile devices, giving them greater visibility into queue activity and performance while on the go.

Users can quickly understand the state of their queues, monitor incoming call demand, and make informed decisions about their availability and queue participation without needing to switch to desktop.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Once available, eligible calling representatives and supervisor leads will be able to view real-time call queue metrics directly from the Queues app on Mobile. Users will be able to:

  • Monitor queue activity: View real-time metrics to understand current call volumes and queue conditions.
  • Track incoming call demand: See key metrics such as calls waiting, calls presented, and calls answered.
  • Stay informed about queue performance: Access operational metrics for their assigned call queues without switching to desktop.
  • Make informed decisions: Use real-time queue information to better understand call demand and manage their availability and queue participation.

The metrics available to users will depend on their role and existing permissions. Calling representatives will have visibility into the metrics available to them, while supervisor leads will have access to additional queue information based on their permissions.

This feature extends the existing real-time queue metrics experience to Mobile and does not change how call queues are configured or managed.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No new admin action is required before rollout. We recommend that you:

  • Review the license assignments for users who need access to the Queues app on Mobile.
  • Ensure that calling representatives and supervisor leads have the appropriate permissions to view queue metrics.
  • Inform your help desk and users about the availability of real-time queue metrics on Mobile, and update internal training and support materials as needed.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft SharePoint: Agent Chat web part to bring Copilot agents into SharePoint pages

We're introducing the Agent Chat web part in SharePoint, allowing organizations to embed their existing Microsoft 365 Copilot agents directly into SharePoint pages. This helps organizations make agents easier to discover and use by bringing conversational AI into familiar intranet experiences, alongside relevant information, instructions, and resources.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.

General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.

General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by late March 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: SharePoint page authors who want to embed Copilot agents. Users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and access to the configured agent.

Platforms/Services: SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Studio.

What will happen: SharePoint page authors can add the Agent Chat web part to pages using the standard page editing experience. Authors can select published agents already available to them in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Users can interact with agents directly from SharePoint pages and continue conversations in a full-screen chat experience. Organizations can place agents alongside relevant SharePoint content to help users discover and engage with them. Existing SharePoint page permissions and agent access permissions remain independent. Adding an agent to a page does not automatically grant users access to that agent. SharePoint page content is not automatically passed to the agent.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout. The Agent Chat web part becomes available as part of the rollout.We recommend informing SharePoint page authors and support teams about this capability and reviewing the documentation: Use Agent Chat web part in SharePoint.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance impact is expected for this change. SharePoint does not store Copilot agent chat data or change how agent data is processed.

 Next slide preview: A preview of the next slide or animation, so presenters can see what's coming.

 Slides only: A simpler view focused on the current slide.

 To change the layout, the presenter selects "Change layout" while presenting. Layouts only change what the presenter sees. Attendees' view of the presentation isn't affected.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Backup: Full workload backup for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We are introducing Full Workload Backup for Microsoft 365 Backup, a new capability that allows admins to quickly protect an entire workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange) with a single policy. This feature automatically includes all existing and newly created artifacts that are not already covered by custom policies, helping organizations improve data protection coverage, reduce administrative overhead, and ensure continuous backup for critical business data at scale.

This enhancement supports enterprise-ready data protection and automation, enabling organizations to safeguard content more efficiently while maintaining control through existing policy configurations.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 464990.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early July 2026 and expect to complete by mid-July 2026.
  • General Availability: We will begin rolling out in January 2027 (previously mid-September 2026) and expect to complete by end of February 2027 (previously mid-October 2026).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Admins managing Microsoft 365 Backup policies
  • Organizations currently using or planning to use Microsoft 365 Backup

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Backup
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Exchange Online

What will happen:

  • A new option to back up all artifacts within a selected workload will be available.
  • Admins can enable Full Workload Backup per workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange).
  • All eligible artifacts not covered by existing custom backup policies will be automatically protected.
  • Newly created artifacts will be included in backup coverage automatically on subsequent runs.
  • Existing custom backup policies will continue to take precedence and remain unchanged.
  • Admins can upload a CSV file to exclude specific artifacts.
  • The feature is available by default but requires admin configuration to enable.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate action is required before rollout.

After rollout, we recommend that you:

  • Review your current Microsoft 365 Backup policies and coverage.
  • Evaluate whether Full Workload Backup aligns with your data protection strategy.
  • Inform backup administrators about this new capability.
  • Update internal documentation if you manage backup procedures.

To enable the feature:

  1. Go to the Microsoft 365 Backup dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  2. Select the workload you want to protect and choose the option to back up all artifacts. 
  3. (Optional) Upload a CSV file on the Exclude sites step to exclude specific sites from the scope of the policy. 
  4. Review the coverage summary and confirm to create the Full Workload Backup policy. 

Learn more:

  • Create, view, and edit backup policies in Microsoft 365 Backup | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout begins) 
  • Overview of Microsoft 365 Backup | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout begins)

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: External presenter support for event group chat
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are adding support for external presenters in event group chat, the private chat used by organizers, co-organizers, and presenters for coordination during an event or structured meeting. This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in late March 2027 (previously early December 2026) and is expected to complete by mid-April 2027 (previously early January).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters using event group chat in meetings or events, including external presenters.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Event group chat
  • Meetings and events with the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled

What will happen

  • External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.
  • The meeting or event must have the Enable Green room Teams meeting option enabled to use event group chat. 
  • External user collaboration must be enabled for external presenters to use this functionality.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change store new customer data?

  • No. Expected changes on the client will only correct the tenantId to the external federated presenter's own tenant.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?

  • Yes. External federated presenters can now read and post in the event group chat. That includes messages written before they joined, if the thread shows history. The presenter's stored tenantId also changes from the organizer's tenant to the presenter's own tenant.

Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?

  • Yes. We are adding a new cross-tenant chat path between the organizer's tenant and external presenters. Both tenants must allow external access.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. External presenters' messages fall under existing federated-chat handling.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: new guided Copilot onboarding experience
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: We have updated this post as a reminder. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

To help organizations increase Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption and build user confidence, we are introducing a new admin-led Copilot onboarding experience for Frontier participants. This guided, in-product experience helps users learn how to use Copilot through role-based activities within the Copilot app. The experience is tailored to the user’s familiarity with Copilot and their license assignment, helping users build confidence through relevant, guided examples while giving organizations control over how onboarding is introduced. This supports Personal and Team Productivity by helping users learn how to use Copilot effectively in their daily work.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously early November).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 admins participating in the Frontier program who want to provide guided Copilot onboarding to their users.
  • Users for whom the onboarding experience has been enabled and shared.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Learning Agent
  • Viva Learning (reporting)

What will happen

  • This is a new, optional onboarding experience that does not change, replace, or retire existing Microsoft 365 Copilot functionality.
  • The experience is disabled by default and must be enabled by an admin with the Global Administrator, Knowledge Administrator, or AI Administrator role. Admins can enable the experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and include their organization's AI policy as part of the onboarding experience.
  • After enabling onboarding, admins can share the experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. When users open the onboarding deep link, the Copilot app launches in the preferred destination set by the admin that shared the experience, such as the Copilot app for Windows, Copilot on the web, or Copilot in Teams.
  • Learning Agent automatically starts the onboarding experience, which takes approximately 5 to 10 minutes to complete, and is personalized based on the user's role, work context, familiarity with Copilot, and license assignment.
  • The Starter journey collects information from the user to personalize the onboarding experience.
  • The Premium journey uses available work and role context to provide relevant examples of how the user can apply Copilot to their work. This journey is only available to users with a Copilot Premium license.
  • If desired, admins with the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role can access and use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.

Starter journey Copilot onboarding experience

Premium journey Copilot onboarding experience

Microsoft 365 admin center Copilot onboarding flyout menu

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required unless you want to enable Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding for your organization during the Frontier rollout. If you plan to use the experience:

  • Ensure Learning Agent and Microsoft 365 Copilot are enabled for targeted users who will participate in the onboarding experience.
  • In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot settings > Microsoft 365 Copilot onboarding and enable the experience.
  • Review your organization's AI policy and determine whether you want to include it in the onboarding experience.
  • Share the onboarding experience with users by using the provided email template or onboarding deep link. We recommend that you share the onboarding experience with new or inexperienced users to help them learn how to use Copilot in their role.
  • If you want to view reporting and have the Global Administrator or Knowledge Administrator role, use Viva Learning reporting to review onboarding completion.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Copilot Code is rolling out in Frontier
item.description:
Update November 17, 2026: Copilot Code is expanding to mobile and Mac, and local Sandbox is rolling out for enablement. We’ve also added guidance for admins managing local Sandbox policies and local execution. 

What’s new 

  • Mobile: Copilot Code is expanding to the Microsoft Copilot mobile app on iOS and Android for Frontier customers. Users can start and continue cloud sessions, follow progress, respond to approval requests, and review results from their mobile device. Local sessions aren’t available on mobile. 
  • Mac: Copilot Code is expanding to the Microsoft Copilot desktop app on Mac. Admins should validate the supported app and update channel and confirm tenant enablement before deployment. 
  • Local Sandbox on Windows: Local Sandbox is now available for enablement. It limits Copilot Code and the processes it starts to permitted file and network access. For organizations that haven’t configured a Sandbox policy, Sandbox is initially off by default, and users can change the setting. Beginning in late November 2026, Sandbox will be on by default, and users won’t be able to turn it off. An explicit admin policy takes precedence over these defaults.
  • GitHub Copilot CLI: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users in the Frontier program can sign in to GitHub Copilot CLI with their Microsoft 365 account, without requiring a GitHub account, and use Copilot Credits to access supported models. The experience is off by default and must be enabled by an admin in Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Usage is billed in Copilot Credits and requires usage-based billing and a spending policy that includes Code. 

Resources 

  • https://aka.ms/copilot-code-docs 
  • GitHub Changelog post

[What and Why:]

Copilot Code is an AI-powered coding experience in Microsoft Copilot that helps people turn ideas into trackers, dashboards, apps, and other solutions using natural language. Work IQ grounds what they build in emails, meetings, documents, chats, and connected data.

People closest to a problem can build the solution they need while your organization maintains control. Published apps run on Copilot Managed Runtime and inherit your organization’s governance, security, and management controls.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Copilot Code: Begins with the Frontier program in late October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users in the Frontier program who have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and are enabled for usage-based billing.
  • Microsoft 365 admins who manage the Copilot app, spending policies, and usage-based billing.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Copilot app on Windows
  • Microsoft Copilot on the web
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Copilot Managed Runtime
  • Work IQ
  • GitHub, when enabled

How admin settings control access

Copilot Code uses usage-based billing. To use Copilot Code, users need:

  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • A spending policy.

By default:

  • Local coding sessions are disabled by default. Admins can allow local coding on PC by setting Code execution location to Cloud and local in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Users covered by a spending policy where the setting "Allow new Agents and services as they become available" is enabled automatically receive access to Code through that spending policy.

For more information about Allow new agents and services setting, see MC1470425.

  6. Decide whether users should have cloud-only coding or cloud and local coding. Local coding is off by default.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Copilot Managed Runtime expands app building at general availability
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime is an IT-governed platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary. It supports app creation in Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio, Copilot Code, and the Copilot Managed Runtime CLI. Apps can use organizational data through connectors permitted by your organization's policies, and admins can manage apps through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime, introduced in public preview in September 2026 (MC1469329), will become generally available. App building in Copilot Cowork will no longer be limited to the Microsoft Copilot Frontier Program.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Rollout began in September 2026 and is expected to be complete by mid-November 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to be complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Licensed users who build or run apps hosted on Microsoft Copilot Managed Runtime and admins who manage those apps, environments, governance policies, and Copilot Credits

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Copilot Cowork
  • Microsoft Copilot Studio
  • Microsoft Copilot Code (Frontier)
  • Copilot Managed Runtime CLI
  • Power Platform environments

What will happen

  • Copilot Managed Runtime will no longer be a preview feature.
  • Licensed users can build apps in Copilot Cowork without participating in the Microsoft Copilot Frontier Program.
  • Makers will continue to build in personal environments that are created when first needed and reused afterward.
  • Environment routing is enabled for Copilot Managed Runtime. If your tenant has no routing rules, users are routed to personal environments in the default environment group. Existing routing rules aren't changed.
  • Personal environments inherit the default environment group's connector, content security, and sharing policies. Makers can't override these policies. Admins can manage them under Apps > Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Sharing an app provides access to the app but doesn't provide access to its underlying data.
  • Draft and published apps appear under Apps > All apps, where admins can review app information and perform lifecycle operations such as blocking and deleting apps.

[Action required and recommendations]

Before general availability:

  • Set up Copilot Credits: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost management and create a spending policy that covers all users and includes Copilot Managed Runtime. Note: A small per-user monthly limit, such as 100 Copilot Credits (US$1), covers typical use. Add policies with higher limits for groups that use apps more frequently. Users with a Power Apps Premium license can run apps without a spending policy.
  • Enable makers: For Copilot Cowork and Copilot Code, include makers in an applicable spending policy. For Copilot Studio, allocate credits to the environments where makers build.
  • Review governance: Review policies for personal environments, connectors, content security, and app sharing, as well as apps built during public preview.
  • Communicate the change: Let your organization and maker community know that app building in Copilot Cowork and Copilot Code is expanding beyond the Microsoft Copilot Frontier Program.

[What and why]

We are updating the OneDrive sync app for Windows and Mac to exclude new folders named node_modules from syncing by default, beginning December 14, 2026. This change extends OneDrive's existing default exclusion list, which includes .db-wal files, as mentioned in MC1457838 on October 5, 2026.

JavaScript and Node.js projects can generate tens of thousands of small dependency files in node_modules folders. This change is intended to improve sync performance and reduce unnecessary storage and bandwidth usage. Developers can rebuild these folders using their package manager.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin on December 14, 2026, and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Windows
  • OneDrive for Mac

What will happen

  • New node_modules folders: OneDrive will exclude newly created folders named node_modules from syncing by default. These folders will remain on the device and will not upload to OneDrive.
  • Folder name matching: The exclusion applies to folders named exactly node_modules, regardless of capitalization.
  • Existing node_modules folders: Folders that are already syncing will continue to sync. OneDrive will not remove existing content from the cloud or devices.
  • User experience: Users will not receive prompts. Excluded folders will continue to function locally but will not be available through OneDrive on the web or other devices.
  • Administrative controls: Administrators can use existing OneDrive sync policies to turn off the default exclusion list if their organization needs these folders to sync.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization wants to use the new default behavior. If your organization needs node_modules folders to continue syncing, configure the appropriate OneDrive sync policies before December 14, 2026.

We recommend that you update your helpdesk and developer guidance to reflect the new default behavior and notify developers who maintain code projects in OneDrive-synced locations.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) OneDrive transitions to the cloud.microsoft domain
item.description:
Updated November 17, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

OneDrive is transitioning to the cloud.microsoft domain. Users will start seeing new URLs shown in the examples below as a part of their OneDrive experiences. Existing links continue to work — both domains will operate side by side indefinitely. 

As part of this transition, OneDrive URLs will change: 

  • Previous domain: contoso-my.sharepoint.com/
  • Unified domain: onedrive.cloud.microsoft/

This change aligns OneDrive with the broader Microsoft cloud domain strategy, creating a more consistent and recognizable experience across Microsoft 365 services. This update simplifies how users identify trusted Microsoft endpoints while maintaining compatibility with existing URLs and integrations.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We began rolling out in early September 2026 (previously end of July) and expect to complete by end of September 2027 (previously early August 2026).

  • We began enabling the early production tenants in early September, with the broader worldwide rollout continuing gradually over approximately one year. As a result, customers should not expect to see this change immediately in their tenants once GA is announced.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • All users accessing OneDrive
  • Admins managing Microsoft 365 environments, network configurations, and custom solutions

Platforms/Services:

  • OneDrive(web primarily)

What will happen:

For users: 

  • Users will start seeing the cloud.microsoft domain in their OneDrive experiences (e.g., onedrive.cloud.microsoft instead of contoso-my.sharepoint.com).  
  • When users access content from geos different than their own, they will see a globe icon. 
  • No changes to file access, sharing, or collaboration functionality.  
  • The previous domain and unified domain will continue to exist side by side. Existing links will continue to work.  

For admins: 

  • No changes to admin functionality. 
  • The SharePoint URLs used for file storage and APIs remain unchanged (e.g., contoso-my.sharepoint.com continues to work for API calls).
  • Important: Organizations with custom solutions that rely on OneDrive URL patterns should review those dependencies. Official Microsoft APIs (Microsoft Graph) will continue to function without changes. Custom solutions that parse or hardcode browser URLs may require updates. 

What is NOT changing: 

  • Existing links and bookmarks will continue to work. Links to previous domains are backwards compatible and will remain supported.
  • There are no forced redirects from legacy URLs. Both domains will work side-by-side during and after the transition.
  • SharePoint site URLs (e.g., contoso.sharepoint.com) are not affected by this change.
  • Microsoft Graph APIs and other official APIs are not changing.
  • File ownership, permissions, and sharing settings are unchanged. 
  • Consumer OneDrive URLs are not changing at this time and remain on live.com domain 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No immediate action is required, but we recommend the following:

  • Review any custom solutions that depend on OneDrive URL patterns.
  • Ensure network rules allow traffic to *.cloud.microsoft.
  • Update internal documentation and training materials with the new URL format.
  • Prepare helpdesk teams for user questions about URL changes.
  • Educate users to recognize the cloud.microsoft domain as trusted

Optional administrative considerations:

  • Review tenant allow list settings for external sharing
  • Evaluate Tenant Restrictions v2 if applicable to your organization
  • Consider upcoming capabilities such as anonymous link controls

Learn more: Configure Tenant Restrictions - Microsoft Entra ID - Microsoft Entra External ID | Microsoft Learn

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?

  • Yes. Eligible users can ask natural-language questions, refine analyses through follow-up requests, and generate summaries, visualizations, reports, and presentations.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. Interactive insights does not modify underlying personal records or replace existing access, export, correction, or deletion workflows. Users can delete their analysis sessions, and administrators can delete sessions for users, subject to applicable retention and hold requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Agent 365 Business Analytics: Introducing Access Management
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing Access Management for Agent 365 Business Analytics, previously Copilot Analytics, so admins can manage who has access and what they can do directly in the product. The new Access Management experience brings role assignment and permissions into one place for Global administrators, AI administrators, and Viva Insights administrators. This simplifies the previous experience that involved managing access across Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center and in-product Manager Settings.

At the core of the new model are Access Policies, rules that define the capabilities users can access and the data they can see. Each policy combines two components:

  • Permission Set: Defines what users can do, such as access dashboards and reports, export data, customize reports and publish them.
  • Partition: Defines the population and datasets users can access, determining whose data they can see and which insights are available.

Admins can assign access policies to individual users, Microsoft Entra security groups, Group Managers, or define users based on organizational attributes. Existing role assignments such as Chief officers, Managers, and Analysts will continue to work, with users automatically transitioned to the corresponding system-defined access policies.

The existing Viva Insights Web App Delegation VFAM will continue to control who can use delegation. With the new access model, delegation within a custom partition will mirror the leader’s effective access for that partition. A delegate will never receive more access than the leader and, as the leader receives new access or permissions within that partition, the delegate’s access will automatically stay in sync without requiring the delegation to be updated.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early January 2027 and is expected to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Global administrators, AI administrators, and Viva Insights administrators who manage access to Agent 365 Business Analytics.
  • Users whose access is managed through access policies.

Platforms and services

  • Agent 365 Business Analytics
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Entra security groups
  • Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM)

What will happen

  • Global administrators, AI administrators, and Viva Insights administrators will assign roles and permissions directly in Agent 365 Business Analytics.
  • Global administrators, AI administrators, and Viva Insights administrators will receive Identification and export features automatically. 
  • Access policies will combine a permission set, which determines what users can do, with a partition, which determines which people and datasets users can see.
  • Policies can be assigned to individual users, Microsoft Entra security groups, or, for group managers, organizational attributes.
  • Existing role assignments will continue to work, and users will automatically move to system-defined access policies.
  • Explicit grants in new access policies can override tenant-level VFAM restrictions.
  • The IdentifiableOutput, Analyst Report Publish, CopilotDashboard Export, Report Customization and Agent Metrics Export VFAM settings will be controlled via permission sets.
  • The existing Viva Insights Web App Delegation VFAM will continue to control who can use delegation.

[Action required and recommendations]

For tenants with the default state of the IdentifiableOutput, Analyst Report Publish, CopilotDashboard Export, Report Customization and Agent Metrics Export VFAM settings, we recommend that you:

  • Review your current VFAM settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center and check who has the Copilot dashboard, Agent dashboard, export, identifiability, and publish enabled or restricted.
  • Confirm who holds the Global administrator, AI administrator, and Viva Insights administrator roles. These admins will manage Access Management.
  • Review access lists for leaders, group managers, and analysts against your organization's privacy requirements.
  • Review your partitions and identification, minimum group size, user-level export, and insights settings.
  • Chief officers can now view and export company-wide Cost insights. Select Edit for the Chief Officer access policy in the Access management page, and enable the toggle. This gives chief officers and their delegates access to all of the spend and billing measures for usage-based billing services.
  • Managers can view and export team-wide Cost insights by default. To disable Cost insights for managers, you can turn off the toggle by clicking on 'Edit policy' for the Manager access policy.

Important notice for tenants who have modified the default state any of the previously mentioned VFAM settings by creating custom policies:

  • In addition to the above, we also recommend that you set up matching access policies within 30 days of availability of the new access management.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation prior to rollout.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use case classification for agent sessions and Copilot Cowork (Frontier public preview)
item.description:
[What and why]

Use case classification is coming to public preview for Microsoft Frontier public tenants. This capability classifies agent sessions and user activity in Microsoft Copilot Cowork against a predefined taxonomy of use cases.

These insights help organizations understand the work performed by users and agents, identify which use cases consume the most AI credits, and find opportunities to consolidate agents and optimize AI investments. Use case classification also provides the foundation for AI value metrics, including AI value for Copilot Cowork.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Frontier preview: Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Frontier public tenants using eligible agents or Microsoft Copilot Cowork

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft Copilot Cowork
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Copilot Studio
  • Azure AI Foundry
  • Agent 365 Connected platforms

What will happen

Use case classification will be enabled by default for eligible Frontier tenants and users. AI value calculations, currently limited to Copilot Cowork user activity, will also be enabled by default.

The capability supports two types of activity:

Agent sessions

  • Sessions from agents built with Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry, declarative agents, and third-party agents registered through Agent 365 Connected platforms will be classified according to the work performed.
  • Eligible admins can review use cases and session counts in the agent Activity tab and Agent Map in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • These classifications are not shared with end users or agent makers.

Work activity in Microsoft Copilot Cowork

  • User activity in Copilot Cowork will be assigned to the predefined use case that most closely represents the work performed.
  • Eligible admins can view aggregated Cowork use cases, associated costs, and estimated value in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Cost Management > Consumption > Use cases.
  • Admins can disable classification for specific users or groups, and eligible users can opt out through the Data and privacy tab in their Microsoft profile editor.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. Use case classification and AI value calculations will be enabled by default for eligible Frontier tenants and users.

Global Administrators and AI Administrators can manage these capabilities through three independent controls:

  • Agent session classification: Turn off classification for the entire tenant in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Settings > Activity classification.
  • Copilot Cowork work activity classification: Use Feature access management to create a policy that disables classification for the entire organization, specific groups, or individual users. Eligible users can also opt out through the Data and privacy tab in their Microsoft profile editor.
  • AI value calculations: Turn AI value metrics on or off and customize the inputs used to calculate AI value in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Settings > AI value. AI value calculations based on use case classifications are currently limited to Copilot Cowork.

We recommend that admins:

  • Review the available classification and AI value controls to determine whether changes are needed to align with organizational requirements.
  • Consider notifying users about work activity classification and the available opt-out option.

Additional considerations:

  • When classification is turned off, it stops within one day. Existing classification results are hidden, not deleted.
  • If classification is turned back on, it resumes from that point without classifying activity from the period when it was disabled.
  • Classifications use a predefined taxonomy rather than tenant-specific categories, so confidential project names are not surfaced as use cases.
  • Individual user classifications are not visible to other people. Organization leaders see work activity use cases only as aggregated insights.
  • Classifications are directionally accurate and intended to identify organizational trends, not audit individual interactions.

Learn more

  • Manage Task Inferencing in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Support
  • Understand business use cases for agents in Microsoft 365 admin center (Frontier) | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

This change introduces AI-based classification of agent sessions and Copilot Cowork activity, with associated reporting and administrative controls.

Organizations should review these capabilities and controls against their privacy and compliance requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: Continue using models after reaching usage limits with Copilot Credits
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We’re introducing the option to continue using models in Copilot Chat and Office through usage-based billing (UBB) after reaching the usage limits included in a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. After reaching a limit, users can continue with Auto without consuming Copilot Credits or, if they have UBB enabled, can continue with the selected model by consuming Copilot Credits. New credit indicators in the UI help users understand when their work consumes Copilot Credits, while spending policies give administrators control over access and spending.

This capability was originally announced in MC1479276 and is rolling out alongside the models available only through usage-based billing announced in MC1519122.

Additionally, models offered in Chat and Word, Excel, and PowerPoint will now be visible in the model picker. Models that a user does not have access to will be greyed out and users will not be able to select them.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Frontier: Rolling out now.
  • General availability: Planned for early December 2026 in the Worldwide production cloud.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: End users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. To use models with usage-based billing in Chat and Word, Excel and PowerPoint, users must also have access to available Copilot Credits through an applicable spending policy that includes the Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office service.

Platforms/Services: Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint across web, desktop, and mobile.

What will happen:

  • When users reach an applicable model usage limit included in their license, they can continue with Auto without consuming Copilot Credits. Users that have UBB enabled can instead continue with the selected model using Copilot Credits.
  • The new Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office service will be available in spending policies.
  • Access to models with usage-based billing requires the service to be included in an applicable spending policy, with credits available. Users without this access cannot use models with usage-based billing.
  • Existing spending policies with Auto-apply new services enabled automatically include newly supported services as they become available. Policies with this setting disabled require administrators to add the service.
  • A new credits icon helps users understand credit availability and whether their current experience consumes credits:
    • A filled icon indicates that usage is metered and consumes Copilot Credits.
    • An unfilled icon indicates that usage is not metered and does not consume Copilot Credits.
    • Hovering over the icon shows credit usage details and an option to open a pane with additional information.
  • Users can type and submit /cost as a prompt in Copilot to view details about their current session.
  • Users will see models offered in Chat and Word, Excel, and PowerPoint visible in the model picker. If the user does not have access to a model, it will be greyed out, and the user will not be able to select it.

Image of credit icon and usage details.

Image of banner allowing users to continue with credits if they have UBB enabled.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  1. Review existing spending policies. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration and review the policies that apply to your users.  
  2. Confirm service access. To allow usage-based model access, ensure the applicable policy includes Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office, has an appropriate billing method, and has credits available.
  3. Review policy scope, limits, and alerts. Policies can apply to all users or selected Microsoft Entra ID security groups. Confirm the intended audience and configure spending limits and notifications.  
  4. Prepare users and support teams. Explain the choice between Auto and credit-consuming model usage, the new credit indicators, and /cost.

Use these resources to configure and manage access:

  • Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits
  • Manage spending policies and service access
  • Monitor Copilot Credit spending

New way for end users to interact with generative AIYesEligible users can continue using a selected model after reaching an included usage limit by consuming Copilot Credits.

item.title: [stayInformed] Autopilot availability in Frontier
item.description:
[What and why:]

Autopilot will begin a phased roll out within Frontier Public on November 17, 2026. We will give Admins 24 hours notice prior to enabling Autopilot in a tenant.

Autopilot is an always-on, cloud-based personal agent that takes work off your plate and keeps delegated goals moving over time, rather than working one prompt at a time.

Autopilot has its own account and identity, storage and mailbox, and its own remote computer. Access controls, approval guardrails and supported information-protection and compliance capabilities help keep delegated work within approved boundaries.

[Rollout schedule:]

  • Frontier Public roll out begins November 17, 2026.
  • Autopilot rolls out in phases to eligible customers.
  • General availability timing will be confirmed separately.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected

  • Organizations enrolled in Frontier
  • Microsoft 365 admins
  • End users who meet licensing and admin configured prerequisites

Platforms / Services

  • Microsoft 365
  • Microsoft Copilot

What will happen

  • Autopilot becomes available to tenants enrolled in Frontier on a rolling basis
  • Autopilot is OFF by default and not available unless admins complete required enablement steps
  • Users are unable to create an Autopilot unless all admin prerequisites are met

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Pre-requisites

The person responsible for the Autopilot (i.e., the accountable user to whom the agent is assigned) is required to have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and consumption billing enabled. Availability is initially limited to eligible US customers.

 In addition, the following controls are required:

  • Identity platform: Microsoft Entra Agent ID. Provisioned automatically.
  • Isolated runtime environment: Microsoft local (MXC)
  • Immutable audit logs and cost management: Microsoft 365 audit logs and Agent 365 cost management.

The following controls are highly recommended:

  • Access and authorization governance: Microsoft Entra ID Governance (least-privileged access), Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (tool, MCP, and data inspection), and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
  • Data security and insider risk: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management.
  • Threat protection: Microsoft Defender XDR and Dynamic Agent Risk.

For the most secure configuration, the following controls are also recommended:

  • Agentic security: Microsoft Perception (limited preview), Microsoft Entra Conditional Access dynamic controls (limited preview), Microsoft Entra ID Governance dynamic permissions (limited preview)

This licensing and controls guidance applies to Frontier Public Preview. Additional requirements and security recommendations may apply at General Availability.

 How do I get these required and highly recommended capabilities from Microsoft?

  1. Required Microsoft Security capabilities: Intune P1/ME3, Any Microsoft 365 commercial license
  2. Highly recommended Microsoft Security capabilities: Entra Suite, Purview Suite/ME5, Defender Suite/ME5, Agent 365 paid license
  3. Most secure configuration: User-based billing

Admin actions (required)

  • Admin turns on access to Autopilots in MAC
  • Admin sets up a Copilot Credits billing policy
  • Admins enable Autopilot for a security group

User actions

  • Navigate to the Autopilot in the left-hand panel of the Copilot Home experience and select 'Create Your Autopilot'
  • Communicate with your Autopilot in Teams, the Copilot app or Outlook

Recommendations

  • Review this change with security and compliance stakeholders before enabling

Compliance considerations

Autopilot is off by default. Administrators control access through the Microsoft 365 admin center and security-group assignments. Autopilot has its own identity; work performed on a user’s behalf uses that user’s permissions. Automated checks review consequential actions, but some actions can proceed without a separate confirmation.

 Before enabling this Frontier preview, review the Autopilot documentation with your security and compliance teams. Memory is always on in this release, and Microsoft 365 Copilot personalization settings do not apply. Data-protection and audit capabilities have preview limitations; Autopilot conversations are not yet covered by eDiscovery, retention, or legal hold.

item.title: [stayInformed] Agent 365 Business Analytics app experience
item.description:
[What and why:]

We're adding new capabilities to cost management in Microsoft 365 admin center that build on the FinOps for AI capabilities we announced in September in MC1479276.

We're also introducing Agent 365 Business Analytics, a new web app for business leaders and their managers to bring AI spend, usage and value together in one place to answer three questions: What's driving my AI spend? What work is it supporting? Where should I invest next? Agent 365 Business Analytics begins rolling out in Frontier public preview on November 17, 2026.

Changes to the admin experience for Agent 365 Business Analytics, including access management, are covered in a separate Message Center post: "Microsoft Agent 365 Business Analytics: Introducing Access Management". More details on use case classification are covered in a separate Message Center post.

Cost management in Microsoft 365 admin center

    • Spend, use case and value insights: See total spend across Microsoft AI services, including Cowork, with drill-down by user and model (Generally available, November 2026). See what people use AI for, mapped to a taxonomy of more than 6,000 use cases. Measure Cowork value with estimated dollar value, and customize time savings and dollar value for each use case (Frontier, November 2026). Spend and value insights then expand to non-Microsoft agents and AI services (Frontier, December 2026).
    • Forecasting: Forecast spend based on the current burn rate at tenant-level and agent-level. (Frontier, November 2026)
    • Optimization recommendations: Flag agents with unusual activity, such as spend spikes or high volume, and get model routing recommendations. (Frontier, November 2026)
    • Multi-tenant management: Manage spend across tenants. (Public preview, November 2026)
    • Delegated policy management: Hand off spending policy management to another admin (Frontier, November 2026), and then to business leaders (Frontier, December 2026).

Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier public preview)

Highlights of the Frontier public preview include:

    • Cost and forecasting (November): See cost in currency alongside Copilot Credits across licensed and usage-based AI services, forecast spend, and model what-if scenarios such as a per-person spend cap or a different model mix.
    • Service and model insights (November, December for Work IQ API): Drill into Copilot Cowork (including breakout by output type and skills used), Copilot Code, Autopilot, agents, and GitHub Copilot. See which models and providers are used most with flexible time ranges and custom HR attributes.
    • Use case and value insights (November for Cowork, December for other AI services): See what work AI supports and which work drives cost, and track Cowork assisted hours, satisfaction rates, and estimated value based on time and hourly-rate assumptions you set.
    • GitHub Copilot cost and budget (November): View metered spend alongside usage and adoption by organization, cost center, repository and model.
    • Export (November, November end for session-level data): Programmatically export usage and cost data to CSV, Power BI or Microsoft Fabric. Session-level data for custom reporting and chargeback (admins only).
    • Privacy (November): Minimum group size continues to hide aggregated insights for groups below your configured threshold, and existing tenant-level values are preserved.

Agent 365 Analytics is available through https://aka.ms/a365analytics. For more information, please see https://aka.ms/a365businessanalytics/blog.

[Rollout schedule:]

    • Agent 365 Business Analytics: Rollout begins November 17, 2026, starting with Frontier tenants that have 50 or more Copilot licenses. Access expands to all Frontier tenants by December 7, 2026. Access to spend and value data from connected non-Microsoft AI platforms requires Agent 365 and/or Microsoft 365 E7 licensing.
    • Cost management in Microsoft 365 admin center: Capabilities begin rolling out November 17, 2026. Access to spend and value data from connected non-Microsoft AI platforms requires Agent 365 and/or Microsoft 365 E7 licensing.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: Frontier-program organizations in Worldwide environments as rollout reaches their tenant; existing Viva Insights users/admins (roles carry over); admins managing usage-based AI billing and cost management.

Platforms/Services: Web - Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft 365 admin center, Viva Insights.

What will happen:

  • Agent 365 Business Analytics becomes available at aka.ms/a365analytics as rollout reaches each tenant; Viva Insights roles/settings (incl. minimum group size) carry over automatically.
  • For tenants without Viva Insights, global admins, the CEO, and their next two management levels get tenant-level access by default; managers of 10+ person teams get org-level insight access. Cost data for tenant-level access stays off until an admin enables it.
  • Manager-hierarchy data comes from Microsoft Entra ID by default; admins can upload a .csv or use MODIS to override HR attributes.
  • Use case classification and Cowork AI value calculation are on by default for eligible tenants/users (admin-manageable; users can opt out of Cowork classification) - see the separate access-management post for details.
  • Identifiable user-level data is off by default; admins can enable it per user/group via a Viva feature access management policy.
  • Viva Insights will show a banner promoting Agent 365 Business Analytics.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required for the Frontier rollout (staged through Dec 7, 2026). To prepare:

  • Review Frontier program enrollment and who should get preview features: Get started with Frontier.
  • Review who has access, including identifiable user-level data access: Roles in Viva Insights.
  • Review minimum group size and other privacy settings against your organization's requirements.
  • Review use case classification and Cowork AI value settings (see the separate use case classification post).
  • Verify the Microsoft Entra ID manager hierarchy is current, or upload/override HR attributes via .csv or connector.

Additional information: Agent 365 Business Analytics overview, use case insights overview, forecasting/what-if modeling, Cowork value metrics, usage-based billing overview.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data?Aggregates AI spend/usage/value data (e.g. Cowork assisted hours, cost) with organizational data from Entra ID or uploaded HR attributes.
Does the change introduce/modify AI capabilities interacting with customer data?Analyzes Copilot Cowork/Code, Autopilot, agent and GitHub Copilot usage, including use-case classification, to produce insights.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter agent will be generally available
item.description:

Consecutive interpretation in Interpreter for Teams meetings, currently in public preview, is planned to begin rolling out to general availability. This is a new mode in Interpreter that helps meeting participants collaborate more naturally in bilingual conversations. After an eligible meeting organizer turns it on, this turn-by-turn experience interprets each statement after a speaker finishes and then plays the interpreted audio for all meeting participants to hear. 

Similar to other new advanced Microsoft AI experiences, consecutive interpretation will be delivered through usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits. Usage charges can begin after an administrator configures a spending policy and an eligible meeting organizer turns on the experience for their meeting. A Copilot license is also required as a pre-requisite for the organizer of the meeting. 

The existing simultaneous interpretation mode in Interpreter for Teams meetings and Rooms, which is generally available, hasn't changed. It's still a personal listening experience that includes 20 hours of interpreted audio per month through a Copilot license or a Teams Rooms Pro license. Access beyond the hours included is subject to available capacity, limitations, and additional terms.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557180.

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected: 

Organizations that use Interpreter in Teams meetings, including public preview users of consecutive interpretation. 

  • In a meeting, an eligible organizer can select More > Interpreter > Consecutive interpretation (uses credits), then choose the two spoken languages.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams Mobile: Introducing shared call history in the Queues app
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing shared call history in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile, allowing authorized call queue representatives to view calls handled across their queue. This includes missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. By extending the existing desktop experience to mobile, we are helping teams coordinate customer follow-ups, avoid duplicate callbacks, and manage calls more efficiently while working away from their desks.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Representatives and supervisors with access to shared call history in the Queues app, which is included with a Teams Premium license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile, Queues app

What will happen

  • Authorized representatives can view shared call history across their call queue, including missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Shared call history on mobile uses the same administrative settings as the desktop experience.

  • Users can filter call history by resolution status to identify calls that need attention.

  • Users can tap a call to view details, including the caller, call type, time, voicemail or forwarding information, and a timeline of the call's progression through the queue.

  • The system automatically marks missed calls as Unresolved, allowing representatives to identify customers who need follow-up.
  • Users can change missed call statuses to In progress or Resolved. All queue members with access to shared call history can see the updated status, who made the change, and when.
  • Users without shared call history enabled will continue to see only their personal call history.

[Action required and recommendations]

No new administrative action is required for this rollout. We recommend that you inform call queue representatives about the new mobile experience, particularly how to update missed call statuses to avoid duplicate follow-ups.

  • If your organization already uses shared call history, eligible users will automatically receive the mobile experience.
  • If shared call history is not enabled, you can enable it in the Teams admin center by creating a Shared Call History template and assigning it to your call queues. You can grant access to all queue members or restrict access to authorized users.
